Senses.Explanation: To miss it: to let what is immediately at issue pass by without meeting it. Sanjiao Zongyin says that even asking what 'this matter' is has already missed it, and answers Magu's reformulated question with the same verdict. Yuanwu Keqin says the miss occurs in the time of raising an eyebrow; Puzhao Xiaoqin says taking up what is right before one can itself become the miss. Dahui Zonggao tells a questioner that he has missed it without knowing and elsewhere says that opening the eyes misses it and closing them misses it too. Zhenjing Kewen says that merely forming an intention while he comes forward has already missed it. Nanfeng Yunbian answers a question about a matter beyond the standard fourfold alternatives with 'you miss it face to face.' Baima Guixi gives a paired limit: hurry and one misses it, go slowly and one cannot catch up. Baichi Xingyuan contrasts counting that remains plainly exact with casually saying 'I understand,' which misses it. The ordinary verb becomes a recurrent public verdict on timing, attention, and response; no single posture, speed, or verbal formula guarantees against it.
Senses.Note: Frozen-corpus concordance: 1,555 exact hits in 237 files and 232 independent works. One act covers missing, overlooking, and letting the occasion pass. Different triggers—asking, intending, opening or closing the eyes, hurrying, slowing, or claiming understanding—are attested circumstances of the same miss, not separate senses.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Meeting the Source (五燈會元), Sanjiao Zongyin section. After Magu asks what the matter is, Sanjiao Zongyin is the exact speaker who answers, 'You miss it.' The actor-pure KWIC stores only Sanjiao's headword-bearing reply.

Occurrences.Kwic: 乃云。眨上眉毛蹉過。大似開眼尿床。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo (圓悟佛果禪師語錄), hall address. Yuanwu Keqin is the exact speaker saying that the miss occurs in the time of raising an eyebrow.
Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Dahui Pujue (大慧普覺禪師語錄), public exchange. Dahui Zonggao is the exact speaker telling the questioning monk that he has missed it without knowing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 總道我會底，未免等閒蹉過。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baichi (百癡禪師語錄), hall address. Baichi Xingyuan is the exact speaker warning that those who simply say they understand still casually miss it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 我與麼來，你擬心早是蹉過了也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Full Collection of the Five Lamps, volumes 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), Zhenjing Kewen section. In his own hall address, Zhenjing Kewen is the exact speaker saying that by the time a listener forms an intention as he comes forward, the listener has already missed it.

The Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps, volumes 10–25 (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), Puzhao Xiaoqin Mingwu section. Puzhao Xiaoqin is the exact speaker saying that taking it up face to face can itself become missing it.

Continuation of the Orthodox Lamp Lineage (續燈正統), Nanfeng Yunbian section. Nanfeng Yunbian is the exact respondent who answers a question about a matter beyond the four alternatives by saying, 'You miss it face to face.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 只在你眼睛裏，開眼也蹉過、合眼也蹉過。既在眼睛裏，為甚麼却蹉過？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Collected Raised Cases of the Chan School (宗門拈古彙集), Nanyang Huizhong case. The compilation explicitly introduces this as a comment by Jingshan Gao, Dahui Zonggao. Under the quoted-speech rule, Dahui is the exact historical speaker saying that opening the eyes misses it and closing them misses it too.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：急走即蹉過，慢行趂不上。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Strict Lineage of the Five Lamps, volumes 10–25 (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), Baima Guixi section. In his own hall address, Baima Guixi is the exact speaker saying that hurrying misses it while going slowly cannot catch up.
